name: Long Valley-Lake County

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel, Cabernet Franc, Tempranillo and Dolcetto fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon and Zinfandel sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Sauvignon Blanc is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.
